I read the whole file. I also checked how the main declarations are used elsewhere in Mathlib: `ConjAct.lean` (`mem_orbit_conjAct`, `orbitRel_conjAct`, and the lemma identifying `orbit (ConjAct G) g` with `(ConjClasses.mk g).carrier`), and `Subgroup/Basic.lean` (`conjugatesOfSet`, which is built from `conjugatesOf`). I also searched for other definitions of the library note `slow-failing instance priority` and found only this one.

`IsConj` is defined as `∃ c : αˣ, SemiconjBy ↑c a b`, so it builds on `SemiconjBy` and does not compete with it. The `ConjClasses` quotient follows `Associates` by design, as the file comment says, and is not an independent copy of existing API. `conjugatesOf` and `ConjClasses.carrier` are two views of one set; `carrier` is defined by lifting `conjugatesOf`. The `ConjAct` orbit is connected to `IsConj` by bridge lemmas in a later file, so it is not a competing definition. The `Inhabited` and `One` instances on `ConjClasses` are both `⟦1⟧`, which is trivial overlap and not worth a finding. `conj_inv`, `conj_mul`, `conj_pow` and `conj_zpow` are standalone lemmas, which the rubric excludes. I found no avoidable competing concept with a concrete cost. The remaining uncertainty is that I did not read every use of the `IsConj` API.
